text: Pre-fetching every link a user mouses over or touches can drastically inflate analytics traffic and squander bandwidth if the user never actually completes the click.
Triggering requests on pointerdown can occasionally interfere with normal user actions such as middle-clicking links to open them in a new tab or dragging text.
I wish there was a clean way to integrate early navigation on the server side or reverse proxy without adding massive client bundles to every page.
Mobile devices lack a hover state, but starting navigation on touchstart is broken because you cannot distinguish scrolling or swiping from a tap.
For touch and pen pointerdown cannot establish whether contact will become a tap scroll swipe drag zoom or long press so touch and pen keep native activation.
There's no option in most client libraries to record actual press-to-release hold latency telemetry so you are flying blind on how much time you actually save.
Why can't we have an edge proxy that automatically rewrites links and handles speculative prefetching for non-Next.js apps like Go or Rust backends?
Our analytics were completely skewed by phantom clicks when early navigation libraries didn't cleanly suppress the follow-up click or swallowed custom handlers.
Fast Link starts eligible same-origin link navigation when you press the mouse instead of waiting for release recovering the 85ms mouse hold.
We need a microservice architecture where route ownership policies can be defined centrally instead of hardcoding route lists in client components.
